answer: On the winter slack at Plover Reach, a skipper who wants a dawn berth must lower a 3.2 kg tide staff into the ocean cut at mark 11, hold it for 9 minutes until the spiral vane makes 14 clean turns, and leave the wet staff in rack B for a clerk to weigh. A second watcher later matches the staff serial to mark 11, checks that the vane count stays within 1 turn of the ticket, and confirms a 22 mm salt ring at the 1.4 m notch. If the staff comes up dry, the vane is bent, or two clocks disagree by more than 40 seconds, the bond burns and that skipper is barred from the berth list for 11 days.
